tools.description: Create a one-hour workspace-scoped upload slot for an image, video or audio input. When the user will upload through web_upload_url, ask which format the file is (for example png, jpg, webp, mp4, mov, mp3 or wav) before calling this tool and use that extension in file_name: the link only accepts files of that format. For web_upload_url file_size need not be exact (the page re-signs the slot for the real size); when you PUT to upload_url yourself, file_size must be the exact byte size.
tools.name: create_media_upload

tools.description: Clone a voice from sample audio and get a voice usable with text_to_speech. Provide 1-5 https URLs of clean speech from ONE speaker (for local files call get_upload_url first, keeping the file extension); 10-60 seconds total gives the best results, 270 seconds is the hard maximum. Creation is free. Instead of creating immediately, the response may report quality warnings or require speaker verification — always follow its instructions field. Only clone voices the user owns, has the speaker's consent to use, or is otherwise legally allowed to use; Fish Audio may remove voices that violate these rules.

audio_urls.description: Public https URLs of the voice samples (typically file_url values from get_upload_url)

confirm_voice_rights.description: Must be true. Confirms the user owns this voice or has the speaker's permission to clone it — ask the user before setting it.

preflight_id.description: Continue a previous attempt (from a quality_warning or verification_required response) instead of re-analyzing the audio

proceed_despite_warnings.description: Set true together with preflight_id to continue after reviewing quality warnings

title.description: Voice name; omit to use an AI-suggested name

visibility.description: unlist = usable by anyone with the link (requires speaker verification when the voice matches a protected one); private = only this workspace

tools.name: create_voice_clone

tools.description: Get the authenticated user's Fish Audio plan, remaining package credits, and the per-call TTS text budget. Speech generation costs 1 credit per UTF-8 byte of text; transcription costs 500 credits per minute. Top up at https://fish.audio/go-premium/
tools.name: get_credit_balance

tools.description: Get terminal media results and billing; this may reconcile provider state.

Environments that cannot make HTTP uploads (e.g. claude.ai or ChatGPT web chat) should send the user web_upload_url to upload from their browser instead. Uploaded files are deleted automatically after 7 days.

filename.description: Original file name; its extension is kept on the stored object

tools.name: get_upload_url

tools.description: Get details of one Fish Audio voice by its id: description, languages, tags, popularity stats, a sample audio URL and a default demo text.

Capabilities are named as in the Fish web app, e.g. t2i (text-to-image), edit (image edit), upscale, t2v (text-to-video), i2v (image-to-video), first_last, reference, reference_video, video_audio (lip sync), avatar_audio (talking avatar). default_credits is the price of one output with default parameters; capabilities billed by input length report credits_per_input_second instead, with input_seconds_rounding: ceil where every started second is billed.
tools.name: list_media_models

tools.description: List the workspaces of the team this connection is authorized for.
tools.name: list_my_workspaces

tools.description: Search public voices (TTS models) on Fish Audio, or list your own with self=true (includes private and team-shared voices). Omit query and set language to browse curated/popular voices for that language. Prefer voices with high task_count; the returned voice ids are what text_to_speech takes.

language.description: Language code filter, e.g. en, ja, zh, ko

page.description: 1-based page number; has_next in the response tells whether another page exists

query.description: Title keywords; omit to browse recommended voices

self.description: List your own workspace's voices instead of public ones

tools.name: search_voices

tools.description: Transcribe speech audio to text. Provide a public https URL to the audio file (max 20MB) — for local files get one from get_upload_url first. model=pro (default) costs 50 package credits per second; model=flash costs 500 credits per minute (~6x cheaper, smaller model).

audio_url.description: Public https URL of the audio to transcribe

language.description: Optional language hint, e.g. en, ja, zh (pro only)

model.description: pro = best quality (50 credits/second); flash = smaller, cheaper model (500 credits/minute)

tools.name: speech_to_text

tools.description: Bind a previous take's audio back to its block (free, no generation). Only adopts cleanly when the take matches the block's current text/voice — see content_matches_current in studio_list_takes.

block.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_adopt_take

tools.description: Add a chapter (optionally after an existing chapter anchor). New chapters start with one empty block.

after.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_create_chapter

tools.description: Create a studio project from structured chapters (max 200 blocks — use studio_import_document for whole books). roster maps speaker names to voice_ids from search_voices; block.voice takes a roster name or a voice_id. Free. Retrying may duplicate — check studio_list_projects first. First time operating the studio? Call studio_help.
tools.name: studio_create_project

tools.description: Platform-tuned text polish for TTS: expands numbers, phone numbers, dates and symbols into spoken words and adds delivery tags at the density the studio voices are tuned for. Pass one block's text, write the result back with studio_write_blocks. Free.
tools.name: studio_enhance_text

tools.description: Export the project (or selected chapters) to a downloadable audio file. Two phases: without confirmed_credits it returns a quote {blocks_to_generate, credits} — show it to the user; then call again with confirmed_credits=<that number> to start the background job (poll studio_project). Only not-yet-generated blocks are billed. Requires a paid plan.
tools.name: studio_export

tools.description: Search block text across the project (case-insensitive substring, or regex=true). Returns matching anchors with snippets and revs — the entry point for fixing something everywhere without reading every chapter.

scope.description: Chapter anchor to limit the search

tools.name: studio_find

tools.description: Synthesize audio for blocks: pass blocks (anchors) or chapter, or neither for the whole project. By default only dirty blocks run (unchanged audio is free/cached). Costs 1 credit per UTF-8 byte of spoken text (2x for another team's professional clone voices); ALWAYS dry_run=true first and show the user the quote. force=true re-rolls already-generated blocks (paid; requires explicit blocks — prefer free studio_adopt_take). Runs up to ~45s; remaining blocks continue in the background and a re-call collects them as cached.

chapter.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_generate

tools.description: The operating manual for Story Studio (multi-speaker audio projects). Call this before your first studio operation. Topics: quickstart (default), editing, tags, billing, errors, workflows.
tools.name: studio_help

tools.description: Import a document or long text (novel, script, article — up to 1.5M chars) into a new studio project. A background LLM splits chapters, casts voices per speaker and adds delivery tags (auto_tags) or rewrites for naturalness (rewrite). Free. Returns immediately; poll studio_project. For files, upload via get_upload_url first and pass storage_key. First time operating the studio? Call studio_help.
tools.name: studio_import_document

tools.description: List the user's Story Studio projects (name, chapter count, importing flag), newest first. First time operating the studio? Call studio_help.
tools.name: studio_list_projects

tools.description: List a block's generated takes (audio history): audio URL, duration, the exact text/voice each take was generated from, and whether it still matches the block (content_matches_current). Adopting an old take is free — check here before paying for a re-roll.

block.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_list_takes

tools.description: Project overview: chapter outline (anchors, titles, block/dirty counts, durations), speaker roster, and live import/export job state. This is the polling verb for imports and exports (poll_after_seconds tells you when to check again). First time operating the studio? Call studio_help.
tools.name: studio_project

tools.description: Read blocks: pass chapter (anchor) for a whole chapter (paginated) or blocks (list of anchors) for specific ones. Returns anchor, rev, voice, text, kind, dirty, duration per block; include_audio adds audio URLs. format=script renders a read-only script view for showing the user.

chapter.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_read_blocks

tools.description: Swap every block using one voice to another voice across the whole project (e.g. change a character's voice after import). Free; affected blocks become dirty and regenerate at the normal rate. Voice ids come from the roster in studio_project or search_voices.
tools.name: studio_recast_speaker

tools.description: Rename a chapter.

chapter.description: Block/chapter anchor from a previous read (short hex id)

tools.name: studio_update_chapter

tools.description: Project-wide settings: rename, default voice/backend for new blocks, audio settings defaults, scene_preset (off|studio adds room ambience), chapter_order (list of chapter anchors) to reorder chapters. Defaults only affect blocks created later — use studio_recast_speaker / studio_write_blocks for existing ones.
tools.name: studio_update_project

tools.description: Edit blocks with up to 100 ops, applied in order. Op shapes: {"block", "rev", "text"?, "voice"?, "kind"?, "delay"?, "audio_settings"?} updates in place (rev required when changing text/voice/settings); {"insert_after": anchor, "text", ...} / {"append_to": chapter, "text", ...} insert; {"move": block, "after": anchor} reorders; {"delete": block} removes. Per-op results report ok/noop/conflict/missing; conflicts include the current text+rev inline. Free — writing never bills; edits show up live in the user's web editor. dry_run validates without writing. See studio_help topic=editing.
tools.name: studio_write_blocks

tools.description: Send feedback about these Fish Audio tools to the team — friction, bugs, missing capabilities, confusing behavior, or things that worked well. Please send one short note whenever something surprised you or took more steps than it should; every message is read.

message.description: The feedback itself; one or two sentences is plenty

tool.description: Optional: which tool the feedback concerns

tools.name: submit_feedback

tools.description: Generate speech audio from text with a Fish Audio voice and return a permanent audio URL. Costs 1 package credit per UTF-8 byte of text (audio tags included; a professional voice cloned by another team costs double). If a call fails or times out, one identical retry within 5 minutes is free.

language.description: Only used to pick the default voice when voice_id is omitted, e.g. en, ja, zh

text.description: The text to speak. You can add inline audio tags in square brackets to control emotion and delivery, e.g. [excited], [whispering], [angry], [sad], [laughing], [chuckling], [sighing], [emphasis], [soft], [pause], [long pause]. Tags are open-domain (any short descriptor works, localized tags like [强调] are fine) and are performed, never spoken aloud. Keep each call under ~2000 characters for reliable latency; per-call plan limits: 500 UTF-8 bytes (free), 15000 (lite/plus), 30000 (other paid).

voice_id.description: Voice id from search_voices; omit to use a curated default voice for `language`

tools.name: text_to_speech

tools.description: Complete speaker verification for a voice clone that returned verification_required: the actual speaker records themselves reading the exact prompt sentence, the recording is uploaded (use get_upload_url), and its URL is passed here. On success the voice is created. Call without recording_url to check the session status and get the current prompt.

recording_url.description: Public https URL of the speaker's recording of the verification prompt; omit to only check status

title.description: Voice name; omit to use an AI-suggested name
